svg.title: Utley maneuver: finger tamponade of the innominate artery
svg.desc: Original illustration, sagittal cutaway of the neck and upper chest with the front of the patient to the left. The tracheostomy tube has been removed, leaving an empty stoma, and a cuffed oral endotracheal tube sits deep in the trachea with its inflated cuff past the stoma. The clinician's index finger passes through the stoma into the pretracheal space, in front of the trachea and outside its lumen, and presses the innominate artery anteriorly against the posterior sternum and manubrium, while the thumb gives counter-pressure in the sternal notch, pinching the artery between finger and thumb.
